verdict.reason: Re-verified every cited source and the geometry independently; the placement holds. (1) The WI DNR permit-tracking record for FID 246185280 "Vantage WI-1" (https://apps.dnr.wi.gov/warp_ext/AM_PermitTracking2.aspx?id=38402) reads verbatim "Location Address N43430735 W 87861494 Port Washington WI 53074 ... located east of Ozaukee Trail, south of Dixie Road/County Highway P, and west of Interstate Highway 43 ... up to forty-five (45) diesel emergency generators", FESOP 24618528A-F01 issued 06/12/2026 — so 43.430735, -87.861494 is the state agency's own facility coordinate, not a researcher estimate. (2) One Nominatim reverse lookup (lat=43.430735&lon=-87.861494&zoom=16) returns "Highland Drive, Knellsville, Town of Port Washington, Ozaukee County, Wisconsin, 53074" — same town, county and ZIP as the DNR record and press. (3) Overpass fetch of OSM way 1547281515 ("Port Washington (Lighthouse) Data Center Campus", landuse=construction, operator=Vantage Data Centers): my own point-in-polygon test puts the point inside, 462 m from the nearest edge; the area-weighted centroid I computed (43.43197, -87.85764) matches the researcher's cross-check exactly. (4) I downloaded the DNR Environmental Analysis Summary PDF (Dec 2025, 49 pp) and georeferenced Figure 1 ("Location of Vantage's proposed Lighthouse campus") against Lake Drive, the Interurban Trail and I-43: the DNR point lands on the western column of data-center buildings and their generator rows, inside the orange "Proposed Campus" polygon, roughly 1.1 km west of I-43 and 1.24 km south of Lake Drive. The OSM polygon (932 ac by my shoelace calc) does include a NE chunk that Figure 1 shows as "Other Vantage Property", but the point is in the south-west/central building zone that is unambiguously campus under either boundary. (5) Identity: the DNR EA quotes Vantage that the project "is part of OpenAI's Stargate effort, in collaboration with Oracle" and that servers "would be owned and operated by the Oracle Corporation"; Vantage's 22 Oct 2025 release names the Lighthouse campus as the Stargate site; Daily Reporter (18 Dec 2025 groundbreaking) and Ozaukee Press ("672 acres north of Highland Drive and south of Lake Drive between I-43 and the Ozaukee Interurban Trail"; "discontinuing the northern 3,600 feet of Highland Drive") agree. No second Stargate/Oracle site in Wisconsin appears in any source. Precision "exact" is honest: the point sits on the campus's western building cluster. Only nit: the researcher's "40 m from the vacated stretch of Highland Drive" is loose — the point is ~36 m west of Highland Drive's alignment, about 150 m south of the end of the 3,600-ft segment the Plan Commission discontinued; immaterial to the verdict. No Google sources used; WebSearch budget was already exhausted so verification used WebFetch, curl, Nominatim (1 reverse) and Overpass (1 way + 1 roads query).
